Title: Image Resizer
Description: Resize an image to exact pixel dimensions with aspect-ratio lock and Lanczos3 resampling, then save as JPEG, PNG or WebP. Runs in your browser.
Keywords: image resizer, resize image, change image dimensions, resize photo, aspect ratio lock, scale image, resize to width, thumbnail maker
Seo_Introduction: Resize an image to exact pixel dimensions with an optional aspect-ratio lock and download it as JPEG, PNG or WebP. The image is processed in your browser and never uploaded.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
After you pick a file the tool reads its original size and fills **Width (px)** and **Height (px)**. With **Maintain Aspect Ratio** on, changing one side recalculates the other from the original proportions; with it off you can enter any size and the image is stretched to fit. Resampling uses the Lanczos3 filter, which keeps downscaled images sharp.

The output **Format** is preset from the file extension (JPG stays JPEG, PNG and WebP stay as they are, anything else becomes PNG) and can be changed. JPEG and WebP are saved at quality 90 (WebP through the browser's lossy encoder when available), PNG is lossless. Inputs can be PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, ICO, TIFF or TGA; formats the browser cannot display are decoded by WebAssembly for the preview.

Sizes must be whole positive numbers, at most 16384 px per side and 64 megapixels in total; invalid values are flagged before any work starts. Resizing runs in a Web Worker and can be cancelled. Files are named `<name>_<width>x<height>.<ext>`.
Seo_Examples:
**Half size**: a 1920×1280 photo with width `960` and the lock on becomes `960×640`; as WebP it weighs `46.94 KB` and downloads as `photo_960x640.webp`.

**Exact square**: turn off **Maintain Aspect Ratio** and enter `512` × `512` — the image is stretched, not cropped.

**Too large**: a width of `20000` is rejected with “Dimensions are too large: at most 16384 px per side and 64 megapixels in total.”

**TGA input**: a 640×480 `.tga` texture resized to width `320` gives a `320×240` PNG.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Choose an image
Click **Choose file** or drop an image onto the zone. The original dimensions appear under **Original Image**.

### Step 2: Set the new size
Enter **Width (px)** or **Height (px)**. Keep **Maintain Aspect Ratio** on to preserve proportions.

### Step 3: Pick a format and resize
Choose JPEG, PNG or WebP in **Format** and click **Resize**. Use **Cancel** to stop a long job.

### Step 4: Download
Check the new size under **Result Info** and click **Download**.
Seo_Tips:
- Downscaling keeps quality; upscaling cannot add detail and makes the image softer.
- Keep the aspect-ratio lock on unless you really want to stretch the picture.
- For web thumbnails WebP or JPEG keeps files small; use PNG for screenshots and graphics with transparency.
- Very large targets need a lot of memory: 64 megapixels of RGBA is about 256 MB in the browser.
- Metadata such as EXIF and GPS is not copied to the resized file.
ErrorNotImage: Selected file is not an image.
ErrorUnsupportedFormat: This image format is not supported. Use PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, ICO, TIFF or TGA.
ErrorDimensionsTooLarge: Dimensions are too large: at most 16384 px per side and 64 megapixels in total.
